questions.question: A model supports tool calling. Why is that not yet an agent?
options: Tool calling only works with very large models
Something still has to run the tool, return the result, and give the model another turn, repeatedly
Tool calls cannot return text
Agents need a vector database
questions.explanation: Tool calling lets the model request an action. The loop is what runs the action, feeds the observation back, and repeats until a stop condition.

questions.question: In this lesson's loop, what is the normal signal that the agent is finished?
options: The model returns an empty string
The step counter reaches zero
The model's reply contains no tool calls
A tool returns the word 'done'
questions.explanation: A reply without tool_calls is treated as the final answer. The step budget is the safety net, not the normal exit.

questions.question: The model calls calculator with arguments that are not valid JSON. What should the loop do?
options: Raise an exception so the developer notices
Silently skip the call
Return an error string as the tool observation so the model can correct itself
Restart the whole conversation
questions.explanation: Errors are observations. Returning 'error: arguments were not valid JSON' usually gets a corrected call on the next turn; raising ends the run.

questions.question: Why does each tool message carry a tool_call_id?
options: To match each result to its request when the model makes several calls in one turn
To bill tool usage separately
To encrypt the tool output
It is optional decoration
questions.explanation: With parallel calls, results can come back in any order. The id ties each observation to the call that produced it.

questions.question: llama3.2 replied with a JSON tool call written inside content, and the loop stopped after one step. What is the most robust fix?
options: Remove the step budget
Detect tool-shaped text, feed back an error observation telling the model to use tool_calls, and continue
Parse any JSON in content and execute it without checks
Switch the stop condition to 'never stop'
questions.explanation: Feeding back a corrective observation keeps the loop's contract intact. Blindly executing text-embedded JSON skips schema checks and invites injection.

questions.question: Why does run_agent take the model as a plain function llm(messages, schemas)?
options: Python cannot import HTTP libraries inside loops
So the same loop runs with a scripted model in tests and a real model in production
Because Ollama requires it
To make the loop asynchronous
questions.explanation: Depending on a callable instead of a vendor SDK makes the loop deterministic to test and portable across providers.
